`aws_eks_node_group.managed_ng` explicitly lists `depends_on = [aws_iam_role.managed_ng, ...]`, but the node group already references that role through `node_role_arn = ... aws_iam_role.managed_ng[0].arn`, so the implicit dependency on `aws_iam_role.managed_ng` already exists. The explicit `depends_on` entry for the IAM role is redundant. (The instance-profile and policy-attachment entries are NOT redundant and should stay.)

The `gp3` StorageClass uses the `ebs.csi.aws.com` provisioner, which is only registered once the EBS CSI driver add-on is installed. That driver is provisioned by `module.eks_blueprints_kubernetes_addons` (`enable_self_managed_aws_ebs_csi_driver = true`), but `kubernetes_storage_class_v1.gp3` has no attribute reference or `depends_on` expressing that ordering, so it can be created before the driver exists. It should depend on the add-ons module that installs the EBS CSI driver.

The `efs` StorageClass uses the `efs.csi.aws.com` provisioner, which is only registered once the EFS CSI driver add-on is installed. That driver is provisioned by `module.eks_blueprints_kubernetes_addons` (`enable_aws_efs_csi_driver = true`). `kubernetes_storage_class_v1.efs` correctly depends on `module.efs` (via `fileSystemId = module.efs.id`) but has no dependency on the driver that actually implements `efs.csi.aws.com`.

In `modules/kubernetes-addons/prometheus/main.tf`, the `helm_addon` is called with `helm_config.namespace = local.namespace_name` (a plain string) and does not set `create_namespace`, so the Helm release (`create_namespace = false`) is created without any ordering against `kubernetes_namespace_v1.prometheus`. The namespace resource is only consumed by the AMP IRSA modules, so when `enable_prometheus` is on (with AMP disabled) Terraform may run the Helm release before the `prometheus` namespace exists. The Helm add-on should depend on the namespace resource.
